what_it_does: Multimodal AI models — systems that handle both images (or audio) and text — have two very different computational personalities: the encoder part that processes images is compute-hungry (needs lots of math operations), while the language decoder part that generates text is memory-hungry (needs to read large amounts of stored data repeatedly). A single one-size-fits-all chip design handles neither job well. This paper proposes EdgeMM, a multi-core processor that pairs two types of specialized helper chips: a grid of tiny multiplier units (called a systolic array, essentially a conveyor belt of math) for the image encoder, and a digital compute-in-memory unit — hardware that does arithmetic directly inside the memory cells rather than shipping numbers back and forth — for the text decoder. Additionally, it dynamically prunes (zeroes out) less-important weight values in the AI model based on which intermediate values are actually active during a given computation, reducing wasted work. The design was built using a real 22-nanometer manufacturing process, suggesting it is close to a fabricable chip.
